environment.description: Same NestJS service deployed in a Kubernetes pod with a custom init container that sets up a pivot_root-based filesystem namespace. The pod spec uses a distroless Node.js base image with an emptyDir volume mounted at /app. The pod's securityContext sets readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, runAsNonRoot: true (uid 65534), and drops ALL capabilities. A Gvisor (runsc) runtime class is specified via runtimeClassName: gvisor, which interposes all syscalls through a user-space kernel that blocks process.binding and constructor chain access patterns used in vm escape payloads. The pod has no service account token mounted (automountServiceAccountToken: false), and a NetworkPolicy restricts egress to only the internal cluster DNS (kube-dns on port 53) and the specific backend service CIDR. No environment variables containing secrets are injected; secrets are accessed via a CSI secret store driver that mounts them only into /app/secrets/ which is bind-mounted as a FUSE filesystem that returns EACCES for any read attempt from a process whose /proc/self/status shows a parent PID matching the Node.js worker thread pool.

config.runtime: Node.js 18 distroless on GKE with runtimeClassName: gvisor (runsc)
config.filesystem: readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, emptyDir at /app only contains application code and static templates
config.seccomp: gvisor runsc intercepts all syscalls; vm module constructor chain escapes are blocked at the sandbox kernel level
config.network_policy: egress restricted to kube-dns:53 and 10.0.4.0/24 (backend services only)
config.secrets: no env var secrets; CSI SecretStore with FUSE-based access control
config.proc_filesystem: gvisor synthetic /proc with no real host information exposed
